shape: T-junction (3 portals: south, east, west) — asymmetric, two-anchor junction
description: Three-portal T-shape. The junction between corridors isn't a single point — it's split into two anchors connected by a short corridor: the SE junction (where the south and east arms meet) and the W junction (where the west arm ends). The SE junction handles south↔east routing directly; reaching the west arm requires hopping from SE junction → W junction → west gate.

portals.south: spawn_south at (0.08, 23.21) — gate on the south (high-Z) side
portals.east: spawn_east at (23.36, 13.91) — gate on the east (high-X) side
portals.west: spawn_west at (-23.33, 0.00) — gate on the west (low-X) side

traversalNotes: Three-portal T-junction. The junction is asymmetric — the SE corner (where south + east arms meet) is one anchor; the west arm's inner end is a separate anchor. A short connector corridor joins the two junctions.
Direct south ↔ east: spawn_south → se_junction → spawn_east. Two hops.
south or east ↔ west: spawn_(south|east) → se_junction → w_junction → spawn_west. Three hops.

DISPATCH RULE: objectives route through the nearest junction anchor (se_junction or w_junction depending on which arm the objective is on). Don't cross junctions to dispatch an objective — pick the junction in the same arm.
Stages are never physically rotated — all positions are stage-local mesh-space XZ.
